scope: isolated flywheel launcher contacts and ground-rebound calibration

ball.inertia_model: isotropic thin-shell approximation I=2/3*m*r^2; solid-sphere I=2/5*m*r^2 retained as sensitivity case

selected_representation.state_body: one rigid body carries pose, linear velocity, angular velocity, mass and inertia
selected_representation.launcher_contact: analytical sphere-to-finite-cylinder contact evaluated independently for each flywheel
selected_representation.normal_force_law: stateful nonlinear loading/unloading penalty law plus compression-dependent viscous damping; coefficients are in tennis_ball_compliance_calibration_results.json
selected_representation.tangential_force_law: regularized Coulomb traction and equal/opposite wheel torque are implemented, but remain disabled (zero traction) until tyre friction is measured
selected_representation.ground_contact: analytical rigid-plane contact using the same calibrated ball constitutive law, with independent contact state
selected_representation.collision_filtering: native rigid flywheel/ball response disabled only for the analytically handled pair; cradle and ground collisions remain physical
selected_representation.reason: installed Gazebo Harmonic uses DART; ODE surface kp/kd tags do not define a portable calibrated DART ball deformation model

launcher_interface.note: 8 mm exceeds the ITF forward-deformation band at 95.64 N; nip load cannot be inferred from the ITF limit table alone

evidence_limit: The three-axis curves are axisymmetric protocol simulations fitted to published ITF bands, not measurements of an individual physical ball; ball-specific characterization remains unresolved.

acceptance.authorization_scope: normal-contact launcher trials only; tyre-friction-dependent conclusions remain prohibited
